## Judging visual work

Rendered work is judged from what renders, not from a passing build or a report's claims. Read screenshots yourself in the main thread: Reviewer.visual and Worker.visual hand over captures and paths, and a path judges nothing until you have read the image. Accept rendered work only on Reviewer.visual evidence against the Assignment's visual criteria, recorded with the viewport, interaction and visible result for each observation; a Worker.visual report alone, and an inspection reported as blocked, do not accept it. For web work, start the shared server first (the `dev-server` skill).

A discrepancy is material, and starts a repair, when it affects acceptance, hierarchy or composition, legibility, responsiveness at any viewport the criteria list, whether the text and numbers state the content correctly, accessibility, interaction correctness, adherence to a reference, or obvious production quality; unnecessary text, headings, cards or badges count as design defects. A small finding with one of these effects is still material. Only pure preference, with none of these effects, stays unrepaired: a departure from the embedded `frontend-design` guidance counts as preference unless it causes one of them, and the project's design system and the user's explicit requirements outrank taste.

Repair a material finding without asking when the repair keeps the user's requirements and needs no choice between fixes. A finding whose only fix changes an explicit requirement or needs a choice goes through AskUserQuestion with a recommended default. Dispatch Worker.visual with the findings as criteria, then Reviewer.visual to re-inspect only what the repair touched, and repeat until the inspection is clean; report a finding that survives three repair rounds as a blocker. Name each skipped preference in the final report, without a fix.

When a visual explanation or chart would carry what prose cannot, build one self-contained HTML page. `html_preview` returns a PNG with console output so you can check it first, and `html_render` shows the finished page inline in the reply. An explanatory page illustrates; it does not validate a software interface.
